title: Find the Most Common Response
summary: Given a 2D string array of survey responses, remove duplicates within each day's responses and return the most common response across all days.
statement: Given a 2D string array of survey responses, remove duplicates within each day's responses and return the most common response across all days. If there's a tie, select the lexicographically smallest response.
constraints: responses contains at least one nonempty daily list of lowercase words.
A word counts at most once per day even if repeated within that day.
Return the word occurring on the most days, breaking ties lexicographically smallest.
hints: The frequency unit is days, not raw response occurrences, so each daily list must be deduplicated first.
Update a global counter from the set of responses for each day.
Count every word once per daily set, then minimize the key (-frequency, word).
The negative count chooses maximum frequency and the word component implements the required smallest lexical tie-break.
editorial: The negative count chooses maximum frequency and the word component implements the required smallest lexical tie-break.

tests.explanation: After per-day deduplication, good appears on three days and wins.
Bad, good, and ok each occur on two days, so bad wins the lexical tie.
